title: Por qué el cielo es azul

creativeDirection.objective: Explain Rayleigh scattering through a cinematic blend of real atmospheric footage and clear 3D scientific visualizations.
creativeDirection.audience: General Spanish-speaking audience curious about everyday science.
creativeDirection.concept: Move from sunlight and the atmosphere into a molecular explanation, then resolve on the blue sky and Earth's horizon.

visualSystem.typography: Large editorial sans-serif headlines with restrained technical labels.
visualSystem.composition: Full-bleed documentary footage with a compact 3D scientific picture-in-picture and safe-area captions.
visualSystem.lighting: Natural atmospheric light in footage; cool edge lighting and warm solar highlights in 3D.
visualSystem.textureAndMaterials: Cloud layers, sunlight, atmospheric haze and luminous scientific geometry.

creativeDirection.motionLanguage: Use continuous footage with slow reframing, deliberate match cuts, a small animated 3D insert, and short light-wipe transitions. Avoid static title-card pacing.
creativeDirection.soundDirection: Warm cinematic score beneath clear Spanish narration, restrained transition whooshes, and subtle atmospheric texture. Keep footage source audio muted.
rightsAndFactualConstraints: Use only manually reviewed NASA SVS and NASA Image and Video Library clips confirmed as public domain, or other independently reviewed assets with compatible licenses.
Verify each clip's official source page, creator and attribution requirements, license, and selected media file before rendering.
Assign a distinct source clip to each full-bleed storyboard shot when suitable footage exists; do not repeat a source clip in adjacent shots.
Do not present a visual metaphor as literal molecular-scale footage.

shots.purpose: Hook the viewer with the scale and beauty of incoming sunlight.
shots.visual: Documentary footage of sunlight over Earth, sunrise from orbit, or sun rays breaking through clouds.
shots.subject: Sunlight, Earth horizon, sunrise and atmospheric clouds
shots.action: Light travels across the horizon or streams through moving cloud layers.
shots.framing: Wide cinematic establishing shot with visible depth and natural movement.
shots.cameraMovement: Slow push-in or drifting orbital view.
shots.transition: Open directly on motion; carry a bright highlight into the next shot.
shots.audio: Soft atmospheric swell; keep source footage audio muted.
shots.visualProgression: Start: sunrise or sunlight begins at the edge of the frame. Development: cloud and light movement establish scale. End: a bright atmospheric highlight leads into the atmosphere shot.

shots.purpose: Establish the atmosphere as a vast moving layer of air.
shots.visual: High-altitude footage of cloud formations, atmospheric layers, or a view of the blue atmosphere from above.
shots.subject: Atmospheric clouds and the thin blue layer around Earth
shots.action: Clouds drift and atmospheric haze shifts across the frame.
shots.framing: Wide or medium-wide aerial shot with clear atmospheric depth.
shots.cameraMovement: Gentle lateral drift or slow aerial approach.
shots.transition: Match the cloud texture to the molecular 3D visualization.
shots.audio: Low airy texture under narration; source footage muted.
shots.visualProgression: Start: broad cloud field. Development: lateral drift reveals atmospheric depth. End: the blue atmospheric layer becomes the bridge to the light demonstration.

shots.purpose: Give a visual contrast between shorter blue and longer red wavelengths.
shots.visual: Footage of a prism, optical spectrum, blue and red laser light, or a clear light-dispersion demonstration.
shots.subject: Visible light spectrum, prism, blue and red light
shots.action: Colored light moves, refracts, or separates into a spectrum.
shots.framing: Tight macro or clean scientific demonstration with uncluttered background.
shots.cameraMovement: Controlled macro push or short lateral slide.
shots.transition: Cut on the blue portion of the spectrum into scattered light.
shots.audio: A restrained tonal accent marks the color comparison; source footage muted.
shots.visualMethod: Macro footage or scientific light demonstration
shots.visualProgression: Start: white light enters the demonstration. Development: light refracts or separates into colors. End: the blue portion is isolated for the next shot.

shots.purpose: Show blue light distributed through the atmosphere.
shots.visual: Moving blue sky, sunlight through atmospheric haze, or a time-lapse of daylight sky with visible depth.
shots.subject: Blue sky, sun rays, atmospheric haze and scattered light
shots.action: Cloud edges and sunlight shift naturally across the blue sky.
shots.framing: Wide immersive sky shot with a clear blue field.
shots.cameraMovement: Slow upward tilt or continuous cloud drift.
shots.transition: Use a short luminous wipe into the final horizon.
shots.audio: Soft airy sweep; source footage muted.
shots.visualProgression: Start: wide blue sky. Development: visible light/atmospheric movement with the scientific inset explaining scattering. End: sky blue fills the frame and transitions toward the horizon.

shots.purpose: Resolve the explanation with a memorable view of the blue atmosphere.
shots.visual: Earth's curved blue horizon, a sunrise above the atmosphere, or a wide cinematic blue-hour sky.
shots.subject: Earth horizon, atmospheric blue glow and sunrise
shots.action: The horizon glows as the light gradually brightens.
shots.framing: Wide closing hero shot with generous negative space for the final line.
shots.cameraMovement: Slow push-in easing to a calm hold.
shots.transition: Dissolve into the final caption and hold through the end.
shots.audio: Score resolves with a gentle low impact; source footage muted.
shots.visualMethod: Cinematic Earth or sky footage with restrained graphics
shots.visualProgression: Start: dark blue horizon. Development: the atmospheric glow and sunrise grow brighter. End: calm hold on the resolved blue horizon.

acceptanceCriteria: At least three distinct reviewed footage clips are used when suitable licensed selections are available.
Real footage fills the frame while an animated 3D scientific inset remains legible and visually integrated.
All footage layers follow the storyboard timing and use no unreviewed or unsupported licenses.
Spanish narration, word-synchronized captions, and the existing mastered soundtrack remain intact.
No adjacent shots repeat the same source clip unless the storyboard explicitly requires a match cut.

renderStrategy.rationale: This project is specifically a narrated sky/science explainer; the registered composition already provides 3D scientific sequences, narration timing, subtitles and optional footage clips.
renderStrategy.fallback: Use reviewed real sky/atmospheric footage with restrained 2D science overlays if the custom 3D sequence cannot be produced.
